plan: [ In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy with independent private values. Underbidding risks losing when price < value; overbidding risks winning and paying above value if the second-highest falls between your value and your bid. There’s only 1 round, so no learning or reputation effects. Therefore, to maximize expected profit this round, bid exactly my private value, $21, ensuring I win only when the price I’d pay (second-highest bid) is below 21. ]

[ This is strategically equivalent to a sealed-bid second-price auction, since the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid (the clock price when the second-to-last exits). The dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Overbidding risks paying above my value if the second-highest lies between my value and my bid; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With no history and one round, there’s no reason to deviate. I will bid exactly my value, 22, to maximize expected profit. I will win when both rivals’ bids are below 22 and pay the second-highest among them. ]

[ This two-stage auction is strategically equivalent to a second-price auction (winner pays the second-highest sealed bid). With independent private values and risk neutrality, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Overbidding risks winning at a price above my value; underbidding risks missing profitable wins. There is only one round, so no benefit from signaling or dynamic adjustment. Therefore, I will set my sealed bid equal to my value ($13) to maximize expected profit this round. ]
